title.narrative: Promoting Opportunities for Women’s and Youth’s Economic Resilience

description.narrative: Women sustain much of Uganda's informal economy, yet they continue to face entrenched gender inequalities including financial exclusion, unsafe workspaces, limited leadership representation, and widespread harassment. Market women and youth who form the backbone of local trade often operate in overcrowded, unregulated environments with minimal access to skills, digital tools, or fair market opportunities. The Institute for Social Transformation (IST) works at the centre of these challenges. Through the POWER; Promoting Opportunities for Women's and Youth's Economic Resilience project implemented with We Effect, IST enhances the economic resilience, leadership, and agency of women and youth in informal markets. Building on more than a decade of experience, IST provides business and financial literacy, supports digital inclusion through innovations like the Market Garden Application, strengthens cooperatives and VSLAs, and promotes agro-enterprise development to expand income opportunities. IST also invests in gender-transformative leadership, enabling women vendors to participate in and influence market governance and local development decisions. Its revolving fund model and market-based organising strengthen women's access to finance and collective bargaining power. By addressing structural barriers taxation, GBV, unsafe workspaces, and limited policy voice IST contributes to more dignified livelihoods, inclusive markets, and equitable economic participation for women and youth across Uganda.
